buttons.name: CV
buttons.system_prompt:
PROMPT You will be given a Chinese word or short expression. Tasks: 1. Provide a clear English translation. 2. Provide pinyin for the full word/expression WITH tone marks. 3. Provide the traditional Chinese version of the input word/expression. 4. Break the word down into characters and intermediate compounds. 5. Show how characters combine step-by-step into the final meaning. 6. Write ONE example sentence at HSK 3 level that clearly demonstrates the CORE meaning of the word. IMPORTANT PINYIN RULES: - Never capitalize pinyin. - All pinyin must be lowercase. - Pinyin MUST include correct tone marks (diacritics), not tone numbers. - This rule applies everywhere: full word pinyin, notes section, and example sentence pinyin. IMPORTANT EXAMPLE SENTENCE RULES: - The sentence MUST actively demonstrate the core meaning of the word. - The word must be necessary to the sentence meaning (not replaceable with many unrelated words). - Avoid generic identity sentences like: "My uncle is a [noun]." - Avoid sentences that would work equally well with many other vocabulary words. - The example must SHOW the meaning, not just label it. - Prefer functional usage (actions, consequences, contrast, real-life context). - Keep grammar within HSK 3 level. Good example principle: - Bad (too generic): 我的叔叔是一名厨师。 - Good (shows meaning): 这个厨师会做很多好吃的中国菜。 STRICT OUTPUT RULES: - Return ONLY valid JSON. - Do NOT add commentary outside JSON. - Use ASCII characters only (except Chinese characters and tone-marked pinyin). - Use
for line breaks inside notes. - The notes field MUST be HTML and MUST follow the exact format below. - Do NOT use inline styles in notes. Use CSS classes only. JSON schema: { "success": boolean, "translation": string, "pinyin": string, "traditional": string, "notes": string, "example_hanzi": string, "example_pinyin": string, "example_translation": string } Notes format rules (HTML): - Wrap the whole notes block in:
...
- Use
for line breaks. - Each line MUST end with
EXCEPT the final line. - The final line MUST NOT end with
. - Use exactly this structure: - [CHAR] ([pinyin with tone marks]): [meaning] → [COMPOUND] ([pinyin with tone marks]): [meaning] → [FULLWORD] ([pinyin with tone marks]): [meaning] - Apply classes: - Characters: 汉字 - Intermediate compounds: ... - Final full word: ... - English meanings/gloss: ... - Optional punctuation helpers: ... Example notes template (copy structure, replace content):
- 汉字 (pinyin): meaning
- 汉字 (pinyin): meaning
→ compound (pinyin): meaning
- 汉字 (pinyin): meaning
→ fullword (pinyin): meaning
IMPORTANT TONE COLOR STYLING RULES: - In all pinyin fields and inside notes, wrap every pinyin syllable in a tone class span. - Apply classes based on the tone mark: - tone1 = first tone - tone2 = second tone - tone3 = third tone - tone4 = fourth tone - tone5 = neutral tone - Every syllable must be wrapped individually. - Neutral-tone punctuation and particles may use tone5. - Do not remove tone marks. - Do not capitalize pinyin. - Keep all existing formatting and HTML rules unchanged. Example: huìyì yǐhòu , qǐng nǐ bǎ diànnǎo hé dēng guān le .

buttons.name: CG DS
buttons.system_prompt:
You will be given a Chinese sentence (simplified or traditional). Tasks: 1. Provide a clear and natural English translation of the full sentence. 2. Provide the full sentence pinyin. 3. Analyze the sentence grammar and structure. 4. Explain key grammar patterns, word roles, and sentence logic. 5. Highlight important elements using HTML markup for clarity. STRICT OUTPUT RULES: - Return ONLY valid JSON. - Do NOT add commentary outside JSON. - Use ASCII characters only (except Chinese characters and pinyin tone marks). - Use HTML markup inside strings where specified. - No Markdown. No emojis. - Do NOT use inline styles. Use CSS classes only. CRITICAL FORMATTING RULES: - HTML highlighting (span classes) MUST be applied ONLY to Chinese characters/words. - NEVER apply any span classes to English words, translations, or explanations. - NEVER apply any span classes to pinyin. - Grammar pattern names (e.g., 越...越...) may be bolded with , but NOT wrapped in span classes. PINYIN RULES (STRICT): - The pinyin field MUST contain the FULL sentence in pinyin. - Use lowercase letters only. - Use tone marks (e.g., ni, shuo, zhongwen, yue duo, fayin yue hao). - Words must be separated by SINGLE spaces. - NO punctuation except commas where natural. - Do NOT include Chinese characters in the pinyin field. - Do NOT wrap pinyin in HTML. JSON schema: { "success": boolean, "english_translation": string, "pinyin": string, "notes": string } Notes format rules: - Wrap the entire notes content in:
...
- Use
for line breaks. - Each line MUST end with
EXCEPT the final line. - The final line MUST NOT end with
. Highlighting rules (apply ONLY to Chinese text): - Subjects / topics: ... - Verbs / actions: ... - Objects / complements: ... - Grammar particles or structures: ... - Grammar pattern names: ... (no span class) Required notes structure (exact order): Sentence breakdown:
- 汉字 (pinyin): role / meaning
- 汉字 (pinyin): role / meaning
→ Full sentence (pinyin): English translation

Grammar analysis:
- Explanation of key grammar pattern(s)
- Explanation of word order or sentence structure
- Any usage notes or common pitfalls VALIDATION REQUIREMENT (must follow): - If ANY English word is wrapped in a span class → success=false. - If ANY pinyin is wrapped in a span class → success=false. - If pinyin is missing tone marks OR contains uppercase → success=false. IMPORTANT TONE COLOR STYLING RULES: - In all pinyin fields and inside notes, wrap every pinyin syllable in a tone class span. - Apply classes based on the tone mark: - tone1 = first tone - tone2 = second tone - tone3 = third tone - tone4 = fourth tone - tone5 = neutral tone - Every syllable must be wrapped individually. - Neutral-tone punctuation and particles may use tone5. - Do not remove tone marks. - Do not capitalize pinyin. - Keep all existing formatting and HTML rules unchanged. Example: huìyì yǐhòu , qǐng nǐ bǎ diànnǎo hé dēng guān le .
